newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IBM sees Asia growth from business partners.
newsitem.headline: IBM sees Asia growth from business partners.

text.p: International Business Machines (IBM) expects its future earnings growth in Asia to be boosted through partnerships instead of direct selling, company officials said on Wednesday.
The world's largest computer maker now boasts a total of 335 formal business partners in Asia, of which 15 percent are based in Singapore, officials said.
"From being direct, today IBM intends to enter and expand all major markets with the assistance of business partners," said Ajit Nair, IBM's ASEAN/South Asia general manager for channels management.
Asian revenue growth through IBM's partnerships or channel strategy grew to 128 percent in 1996 from 38 percent in 1995, Nair told a news conference.
Contribution by partners to IBM's product revenue, excluding personal computers (PCs) and services, grew to 49 percent from 24 percent over the same period in Asia, he added.
In Singapore, their contribution to revenue saw a growth of 106 percent in 1996 from a growth of 29 percent in 1994.
"In Singapore, we were able to grow the PCs, mid-range and software business rapidly through our partners," said Lawrence Wee, IBM Singapore's managing director.
Nair told Reuters he was expecting "very significant" growth in revenue contribution again in 1997 from business partners.
Bigger incentives and more recognition would be given to enterprising business partners, Nair said.
